questions.subject: COE-01
questions.why: extractor: needs-human: the stored EU documents (Council 9718/25 ADD 1, Decisions (EU) 2024/2218 and 2026/1080) support the Convention's title, the date of 5 Sep 2024, its adoption by the Committee of Ministers on 17 May 2024, the Article 30 entry-into-force rule and the EU's approval of 21 Apr 2026. They cannot show whether five signatories, at least three of them CoE member States, had ratified by 30 Jun 2026, which is what entry into force on or before 14 Oct 2026 would require. Every CoE source (www.coe.int, rm.coe.int, the record's own URLs) returned HTTP 403. A human should check the CoE Treaty Office chart of signatures and ratifications for the treaty and confirm or change status and date_in_force.; official_identifier 'CETS No. 225' is not in any stored file; it rests on the 11 Oct 2026 pass.; date_last_updated is 2026-05-15, the EU ratification date. Under AGENTS.md 5.6 the field is for the last amendment or new version, and one Party's ratification is neither, so it should probably become null, with the ratification kept in the notes. The stored Decision 2026/1080 dates the EU's approval 21 Apr 2026 (published in OJ L 13 May 2026); the 15 May 2026 deposit in the notes is not in any stored file.; If the human confirms the status, the three EU documents can serve as the record's alt-official evidence (level B). Level A needs a stored CoE page.

questions.subject: C007
questions.why: extractor: What exists is one line in a standardisation plan: SAC has approved a project for a recommended national standard on AI deep synthesis security (plan 20264769-T-469, due for approval by 31 Dec 2027), with no draft text. The register covers instruments, including drafts and pending bills, but neither AGENTS.md section 10 nor pipeline/scope-decisions.md says whether an approved standardisation project with no text counts, and a record could say only what the standard will be about. Suggested rule for a human: no record for a plan item; record the standard when its draft for comment is published, and meanwhile mention the project in the notes of CN-02 (deep synthesis provisions). The same list holds about a dozen other AI-related projects (items 7, 9 and 13 to 23), so the decision sets a precedent for all of them.
questions.title: Cybersecurity technology — Security specification for artificial intelligence deep synthesis (planned national standard)

questions.subject: C027
questions.why: extractor: The Senate AI commission's draft 'Ley General para Regular y Fomentar el Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial en México' (chair Sen. Rolando Zapata Bello) has no filed text: no Gaceta or SIL entry is known, and the only sources are Senate press releases about a working draft, which the archiver could not store (HTTP 403). The stored initiative of another candidate (C026, page 35) confirms only that in April 2026 the commission reported working on such a proposal. No rule or precedent says whether a legislative commission's unfiled working draft is an instrument for the register (TH-01 is a draft the government published for public hearing; this one has not been published), and no stored copy supports any field. A human should decide whether to keep it as a lead until it is filed as an initiative, or to record it as a draft once a Senate page can be stored.
questions.title: Ley General para Regular y Fomentar el Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial en México (Senate AI commission draft, chair Rolando Zapata Bello)

questions.subject: C040
questions.why: extractor: Evidence and scope cannot be settled from what exists. The only stored source is a CBS News article (4 Oct 2026) reporting a Truth Social post in which the President announced the 'Super Intelligence Force' after the White House Accord on Super Intelligence (US-27), led by DNI Jay Clayton with the FTC chairman, the Pentagon CTO and the OPM director, reporting to the President and the Chief of Staff. Web searches on 14 Oct 2026 found no whitehouse.gov page, executive order, memorandum or published charter creating the task force; press reports mention a 120-day report and a charter that has not been published. A record would rest wholly on press reports of a social-media post (level C), with no official text to quote for its mandate, legal form or status, and section 10 does not say whether a task force announced only in a post, without a published founding instrument, is an instrument. A human should decide whether to wait for an official document (and keep the lead open) or record it now at level C with a scope_note.
questions.title: Super Intelligence Force (SIF), interagency task force announced by the President

questions.subject: C041
